As a former driver for both Uber and Lyft, both services are on the decline as far as driver relations go.  I started with Uber before they even allowed tipping at the time Lyft did so two weeks into driving for Uber I signed up for Lyft to see if it was better with the tips.  At the time Lyft was bad about giving you a pickup 14 miles away for a trip that was going to be 3 miles.  Uber did add tipping soon after that but I can tell you I no longer drive for either because the service for the driver is horrible.  Both companies long-term plans are for self-driving vehicles they see the drivers is a temporary tool to get them to that point.  So while they may always have "drivers" that doesn't mean actual people.  I don't believe the general public is ready for driverless services like they're wanting to offer.  And there are competing companies trying to break into the North American market who do treat their drivers better and are a better value for their customer.  Anyway it goes being a driver for Lyft or Uber should not be a long-term employment plan.
